6.17.m: Through contact with the ashes on whose body an impure great piśāca, / with its multitude of sins severed, attained the destination of the virtuous through your grace.

6.17.s:
śivayogīti saṅkhyātatrilokavibhavo bhavān |
bhavatkaṭākṣasamparkātpaśuḥ paśupatirbhavet ||
6.17.d:
शिवयोगीति सङ्ख्यातत्रिलोकविभवो भवान् ।
भवत्कटाक्षसम्पर्कात्पशुः पशुपतिर्भवेत् ॥
6.17.m: You are known as a Śivayogī, whose glory pervades the three worlds; / through the contact of your glance, a bound soul would become Paśupati.

6.17.s:
tava tasya mayi pṛcchā lokāśikṣārthamādarāt |
lokopakārakaraṇe vicarantīha sādhavaḥ ||
6.17.d:
तव तस्य मयि पृच्छा लोकाशिक्षार्थमादरात् ।
लोकोपकारकरणे विचरन्तीह साधवः ॥
6.17.m: This inquiry of yours to me was made respectfully for the instruction of the world; / the virtuous wander here to perform what benefits the world.

6.17.s:
idaṃ rahasyaṃ paramaṃ pratiṣṭhitamatastvayi |
tvamapi śraddhayā bhaktyā praṇaveṣveva sādaram ||
6.17.d:
इदं रहस्यं परमं प्रतिष्ठितमतस्त्वयि ।
त्वमपि श्रद्धया भक्त्या प्रणवेष्वेव सादरम् ॥
6.17.m: This supreme secret is therefore established in you. / You too, with faith and devotion, respectfully in the praṇavas alone,

6.17.s:
upaviśya ca tānsarvānsaṃyojya parameśvare |
śivācāraṃ grāhayasva bhūtirudrākṣamiśritam ||
6.17.d:
उपविश्य च तान्सर्वान्संयोज्य परमेश्वरे ।
शिवाचारं ग्राहयस्व भूतिरुद्राक्षमिश्रितम् ॥
6.17.m: having seated and united them all in Parameśvara, / cause them to accept the conduct of Śiva, combined with holy ashes and rudrākṣas.

6.17.s:
tvaṃ śivo hi śivācārī samprāptādvaitabhāvataḥ |
vicaram̐llokarakṣāyai sukhamakṣayamāpnuhi ||
6.17.d:
त्वं शिवो हि शिवाचारी सम्प्राप्ताद्वैतभावतः ।
विचरम्̐ल्लोकरक्षायै सुखमक्षयमाप्नुहि ॥
6.17.m: You are indeed Śiva, practicing the conduct of Śiva, having attained the state of non-duality. / Wandering for the protection of the world, attain imperishable happiness.

6.17.s:
sūta uvāca |
śrutvedamadbhutamataṃ hi ṣaḍānanoktaṃ vedāntaniṣṭhitamṛṣistu vinamramūrtiḥ |
bhūtvā praṇamya bahuśo bhuvi daṇḍavatta-tpādāravindaviharanmadhupatvamāpa ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
oṃ namaḥ śivāya ||
ṣaṣṭhī kailāsasaṃhitā
6.17.d:
सूत उवाच ।
श्रुत्वेदमद्भुतमतं हि षडाननोक्तं वेदान्तनिष्ठितमृषिस्तु विनम्रमूर्तिः ।
भूत्वा प्रणम्य बहुशो भुवि दण्डवत्त-त्पादारविन्दविहरन्मधुपत्वमाप ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
ओं नमः शिवाय ॥
षष्ठी कैलाससंहिता
6.17.m:
Sūta said: / Having heard this wonderful doctrine spoken by the six-faced [Kārtikeya], grounded in Vedānta, the sage, having bowed his form / and having repeatedly prostrated like a staff on the earth, became like a bee sporting at his lotus feet.

Obeisance to the auspicious Gaurī and Śaṅkara.

6.18.s:
śaunaka uvāca |
śrutvā vedāntasāraṃ tadrahasyaṃ paramādbhutam |
kiṃ pṛṣṭavān vāmadevo maheśvarasutaṃ tadā ||
6.18.d:
शौनक उवाच ।
श्रुत्वा वेदान्तसारं तद्रहस्यं परमाद्भुतम् ।
किं पृष्टवान् वामदेवो महेश्वरसुतं तदा ॥
6.18.m:
The sixth [book], the Kailāsasaṃhitā.

Śaunaka said: / Having heard that supreme, wonderful secret, the essence of the Vedānta, / what did Vāmadeva ask the son of Maheśvara then?

6.18.s:
dhanyo yogī vāmadevaḥ śivajñānarataḥ sadā |
yatsambandhātkathotpannā divyā paramapāvanī ||
6.18.d:
धन्यो योगी वामदेवः शिवज्ञानरतः सदा ।
यत्सम्बन्धात्कथोत्पन्ना दिव्या परमपावनी ॥
6.18.m: Blessed is the yogin Vāmadeva, always delighting in the knowledge of Śiva, / through whose connection this divine, supremely purifying tale arose.

6.18.s:
iti śrutvā munīnāṃ tadvacanaṃ premagarbhitam |
sūtaḥ prāha prasannastān śivāsaktamanā budhaḥ ||
6.18.d:
इति श्रुत्वा मुनीनां तद्वचनं प्रेमगर्भितम् ।
सूतः प्राह प्रसन्नस्तान् शिवासक्तमना बुधः ॥
6.18.m: Hearing that speech of the sages, pregnant with love, / the wise Sūta, pleased, his mind fixed on Śiva, spoke to them.

6.18.s:
sūta uvāca |
dhanyā yūyaṃ mahādevabhaktā lokopakārakāḥ |
śṛṇudhvaṃ munayaḥ sarve saṃvādaṃ ca tayoḥ punaḥ ||
6.18.d:
सूत उवाच ।
धन्या यूयं महादेवभक्ता लोकोपकारकाः ।
शृणुध्वं मुनयः सर्वे संवादं च तयोः पुनः ॥
6.18.m: Sūta said: / Blessed are you, devotees of Mahādeva, who bring benefit to the world! / Hear again, all you sages, the dialogue between the two.

6.18.s:
śrutvā maheśatanayavacanaṃ dvaitanāśakam |
advaitajñānajanakaṃ santuṣṭo'bhūnmahānmuniḥ ||
6.18.d:
श्रुत्वा महेशतनयवचनं द्वैतनाशकम् ।
अद्वैतज्ञानजनकं सन्तुष्टोऽभून्महान्मुनिः ॥
6.18.m: Hearing the speech of the son of Maheśa, which destroys duality / and engenders knowledge of non-duality, the great sage was satisfied.

6.18.s:
natvā stutvā ca vividhaṃ kārtikeyaṃ śivātmajam |
punaḥ papraccha tattvaṃ hi vinayena mahāmuniḥ ||
6.18.d:
नत्वा स्तुत्वा च विविधं कार्तिकेयं शिवात्मजम् ।
पुनः पप्रच्छ तत्त्वं हि विनयेन महामुनिः ॥
6.18.m: Having bowed to and praised Kārtikeya, the son of Śiva, in various ways, / the great sage asked about the truth again with modesty.

6.18.s:
vāmadeva uvāca |
bhagavansarvatattvajña ṣaṇmukhāmṛtavāridhe |
gurutvaṃ kathameteṣāṃ yatīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām ||
6.18.d:
वामदेव उवाच ।
भगवन्सर्वतत्त्वज्ञ षण्मुखामृतवारिधे ।
गुरुत्वं कथमेतेषां यतीनां भावितात्मनाम् ॥
6.18.m: Vāmadeva said: / O Lord, knower of all principles, ocean of nectar, O Six-faced one! / How does guruship belong to these ascetics of cultivated soul,

6.18.s:
jīvānāṃ bhogamokṣādisiddhiḥ sidhyati yadvaśāt |
pāramparyaṃ vinā naiṣāmupadeśādhikāritā ||
6.18.d:
जीवानां भोगमोक्षादिसिद्धिः सिध्यति यद्वशात् ।
पारम्पर्यं विना नैषामुपदेशाधिकारिता ॥
6.18.m: under whose power living beings' attainment of enjoyment, liberation, and the like is achieved? / Without a lineage, there is no qualification for instruction for them.

6.18.s:
evaṃ ca kṣaurakarmāṅgaṃ snānaṃ ca kathamīdṛśam |
iti vijñāpaya svāmin saṃśayaṃ chettumarhasi ||
iti śrutvā kārtikeyo vāmadevavacaḥ smaran |
śivaṃ śivāṃ ca manasā vyācaṣṭumupacakrame ||
6.18.d:
एवं च क्षौरकर्माङ्गं स्नानं च कथमीदृशम् ।
इति विज्ञापय स्वामिन् संशयं छेत्तुमर्हसि ॥
इति श्रुत्वा कार्तिकेयो वामदेववचः स्मरन् ।
शिवं शिवां च मनसा व्याचष्टुमुपचक्रमे ॥
6.18.m:
And likewise, what kind is the shaving rite and the bath associated with it? / Explain this, O Master; you ought to sever my doubt.

Hearing this, Kārtikeya, bearing Vāmadeva’s speech in mind, / and remembering Śiva and Śivā in his heart, began to explain.

6.18.s:
śrīsubrahmaṇya uvāca |
yogapaṭṭaṃ pravakṣyāmi gurutvaṃ yena jāyate |
tava snehādvāmadeva mahadgopyaṃ vimuktidam ||
6.18.d:
श्रीसुब्रह्मण्य उवाच ।
योगपट्टं प्रवक्ष्यामि गुरुत्वं येन जायते ।
तव स्नेहाद्वामदेव महद्गोप्यं विमुक्तिदम् ॥
6.18.m: The auspicious Subrahmaṇya said: / I shall explain the yogic investiture by which guruship is attained; / out of affection for you, O Vāmadeva, [I tell] this great secret that yields liberation.

6.18.s:
vaiśākhe śrāvaṇe māsi tathāśvayuji kārtike |
mārgaśīrṣe ca māghe vā śuklapakṣe śubhe dine ||
6.18.d:
वैशाखे श्रावणे मासि तथाश्वयुजि कार्तिके ।
मार्गशीर्षे च माघे वा शुक्लपक्षे शुभे दिने ॥
6.18.m: In the month of Vaiśākha, Śrāvaṇa, or Āśvayuja, Kārtika, / Mārgaśīrṣa, or Māgha, during the bright fortnight, on an auspicious day,

6.18.s:
pañcamyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ vā kṛtaprābhātikakriyaḥ |
labdhānujñastu guruṇā snātvā niyatamānasaḥ ||
6.18.d:
पञ्चम्यां पौर्णमास्यां वा कृतप्राभातिकक्रियः ।
लब्धानुज्ञस्तु गुरुणा स्नात्वा नियतमानसः ॥
6.18.m: on the fifth lunar day or the full moon, having performed morning duties, / having obtained permission from the guru, bathed, and with disciplined mind,

6.18.s:
paryaṅkaśaucaṃ kṛtvā tadvāsasāṅgaṃ pramṛjya ca |
dviguṇaṃ doramābadhya vāsasī paridhāya ca ||
6.18.d:
पर्यङ्कशौचं कृत्वा तद्वाससाङ्गं प्रमृज्य च ।
द्विगुणं दोरमाबध्य वाससी परिधाय च ॥
6.18.m: having washed [the limbs] up to the knee and thighs and wiped the body with a cloth, / having tied a doubled cord and put on two garments,

6.18.s:
kṣālitāṅghrirdvirācamya bhasma sadyādimantrataḥ |
dhārayeddhi samādāya samuddhūlanamārgataḥ ||
6.18.d:
क्षालिताङ्घ्रिर्द्विराचम्य भस्म सद्यादिमन्त्रतः ।
धारयेद्धि समादाय समुद्धूलनमार्गतः ॥
6.18.m: having washed his feet and twice sipped water, he should apply ash / by taking it with the Sadyojāta and other mantras according to the method of smearing.

6.18.s:
gṛhītahasto guruṇā sānukūlena vai mune |
sa śiṣyaḥ sāñjaliḥ svābhyāṃ hastābhyāṃ prāṅmukho yathā ||
6.18.d:
गृहीतहस्तो गुरुणा सानुकूलेन वै मुने ।
स शिष्यः साञ्जलिः स्वाभ्यां हस्ताभ्यां प्राङ्मुखो यथा ॥
6.18.m: Taken by the hand by the benevolent guru, O sage, / the disciple, with hands folded in supplication, facing east as prescribed,

6.18.s:
tathopaveṣṭitastiṣṭhenmaṇḍape samalaṅkṛte |
gurvāsanavare śuddhe cailājinakuśottare ||
6.18.d:
तथोपवेष्टितस्तिष्ठेन्मण्डपे समलङ्कृते ।
गुर्वासनवरे शुद्धे चैलाजिनकुशोत्तरे ॥
6.18.m: should sit thus in a decorated pavilion, / on an excellent pure seat for the guru, covered with cloth, deer-skin, and kuśa grass.

6.18.s:
atha deśika ādāya śaṅkhaṃ sādhāramastrataḥ |
viśodhya tasya purataḥ sthāpayetsānukūlataḥ ||
6.18.d:
अथ देशिक आदाय शङ्खं साधारमस्त्रतः ।
विशोध्य तस्य पुरतः स्थापयेत्सानुकूलतः ॥
6.18.m: Then the preceptor, taking a conch together with its stand, / purifying it with the Astra mantra, should place it favorably before him.

6.18.s:
sādhāraṃ śaṅkhamapi ca sampūjya kusumādibhiḥ |
niḥkṣipedastravarmabhyāṃ śodhitaṃ tatra sajjalam ||
6.18.d:
साधारं शङ्खमपि च सम्पूज्य कुसुमादिभिः ।
निःक्षिपेदस्त्रवर्मभ्यां शोधितं तत्र सज्जलम् ॥
6.18.m: Having worshipped the conch along with the stand with flowers and other offerings, / he should pour into it pure water purified with the Astra and Varma mantras.

6.18.s:
āpūrya pūrvavatpūjya ṣaḍaṅgoktakrameṇa ca |
praṇavena punastadvai saptadhaivābhimantrayet ||
6.18.d:
आपूर्य पूर्ववत्पूज्य षडङ्गोक्तक्रमेण च ।
प्रणवेन पुनस्तद्वै सप्तधैवाभिमन्त्रयेत् ॥
6.18.m: Filling it, worshipping it as before, and according to the procedure prescribed for the six limbs, / he should consecrate it seven times with the praṇava.

6.18.s:
abhyarcya gandhapuṣpādyairdhūpadīpau pradarśya ca |
saṃrakṣyāstreṇa taṃ śaṅkhaṃ varmaṇāthāvaguṇṭhayet ||
6.18.d:
अभ्यर्च्य गन्धपुष्पाद्यैर्धूपदीपौ प्रदर्श्य च ।
संरक्ष्यास्त्रेण तं शङ्खं वर्मणाथावगुण्ठयेत् ॥
6.18.m: Having worshipped with scents, flowers, and other offerings, and shown incense and lamp, / protecting that conch with the Astra mantra, he should veil it with the Varma mantra.

6.18.s:
dhenuśaṅkhākhyamudre ca darśayedatha deśikaḥ |
punaḥ svapurataḥ śaṅkhaṃ dakṣiṇe deśa uttame ||
6.18.d:
धेनुशङ्खाख्यमुद्रे च दर्शयेदथ देशिकः ।
पुनः स्वपुरतः शङ्खं दक्षिणे देश उत्तमे ॥
6.18.m: Then the preceptor should show the mudrās named Dhenu and Śaṅkha. / Then before him, in an excellent place to the right of the conch,

6.18.s:
pūjyārghyoktavidhānena sundaraṃ maṇḍalaṃ śubham |
kuryātsampūjayettaṃ ca sugandhakusumādibhiḥ ||
6.18.d:
पूज्यार्घ्योक्तविधानेन सुन्दरं मण्डलं शुभम् ।
कुर्यात्सम्पूजयेत्तं च सुगन्धकुसुमादिभिः ॥
6.18.m: he should make a beautiful, auspicious maṇḍala according to the rite described for the worshipful arghya, / and worship it with fragrant flowers and other offerings.

6.18.s:
sādhāraṃ śodhitaṃ śuddhaṃ ghaṭaṃ tantupariṣkṛtam |
dhūpitaṃ sthāpitaṃ śuddhavāsitodaprapūritam ||
6.18.d:
साधारं शोधितं शुद्धं घटं तन्तुपरिष्कृतम् ।
धूपितं स्थापितं शुद्धवासितोदप्रपूरितम् ॥
6.18.m: A clean, purified jar on a stand, wrapped with thread, / fumigated, set in place, filled with pure, scented water,

6.18.s:
pañcatvakpañcapatraiśca mṛttikābhiśca pañcabhiḥ |
militaṃ ca sugandhena lepayettaṃ munīśvara ||
6.18.d:
पञ्चत्वक्पञ्चपत्रैश्च मृत्तिकाभिश्च पञ्चभिः ।
मिलितं च सुगन्धेन लेपयेत्तं मुनीश्वर ॥
6.18.m: blended with five barks, five leaves, and five earths, / together with fragrance, he should smear it, O best of sages.

6.18.s:
vastrāmradaladūrvāgranārikelasumaistataḥ |
taṃ ghaṭaṃ vastubhiścānyaiḥ saṅkuryātsamalaṅkṛtam ||
6.18.d:
वस्त्राम्रदलदूर्वाग्रनारिकेलसुमैस्ततः ।
तं घटं वस्तुभिश्चान्यैः सङ्कुर्यात्समलङ्कृतम् ॥
6.18.m: Then, with cloth, mango leaves, tips of dūrvā grass, a coconut, and flowers, / and with other items, he should thoroughly adorn that jar.

6.18.s:
vinyasetpañcaratnāni ghaṭe tatra munīśvara |
hiraṇyaṃ cāpi teṣāṃ vābhāve bhaktyā pravinyaset ||
6.18.d:
विन्यसेत्पञ्चरत्नानि घटे तत्र मुनीश्वर ।
हिरण्यं चापि तेषां वाभावे भक्त्या प्रविन्यसेत् ॥
6.18.m: He should deposit the five gems in that jar, O best of sages, / or in their absence, he should deposit gold with devotion.

6.18.s:
nīlākhyaratnaṃ ca tathā ratne māṇikyahemanī |
pravālagomedake ca pañcaratnamidaṃ smṛtam ||
6.18.d:
नीलाख्यरत्नं च तथा रत्ने माणिक्यहेमनी ।
प्रवालगोमेदके च पञ्चरत्नमिदं स्मृतम् ॥
6.18.m: The sapphire gem, the ruby and gold, / coral and hessonite: this is considered the five jewels.

6.18.s:
nṛmluskamiti samprocya glūmityante'tha deśikaḥ |
samyagvidhānataḥ prītyā sānukūlaḥ samarcayet ||
ādhāraśaktimārabhya yajanoktavidhānataḥ |
pañcāvaraṇamārgeṇa devamāvāhya pūjayet ||
6.18.d:
नृम्लुस्कमिति सम्प्रोच्य ग्लूमित्यन्तेऽथ देशिकः ।
सम्यग्विधानतः प्रीत्या सानुकूलः समर्चयेत् ॥
आधारशक्तिमारभ्य यजनोक्तविधानतः ।
पञ्चावरणमार्गेण देवमावाह्य पूजयेत् ॥
6.18.m:
Then having uttered "nṛmluska" and at the end "glūm", the teacher, / according to proper rule, favorably and with affection, should worship.

Beginning with the Ādhāraśakti, according to the prescribed rules of sacrifice, / having invoked the god through the path of the five enclosures, he should worship him.

6.18.s:
nivedya pāyasānnaṃ ca tāmbūlādi yathā purā |
nāmāṣṭakārcanāntaṃ ca kṛtvā tamabhimantrayet ||
6.18.d:
निवेद्य पायसान्नं च ताम्बूलादि यथा पुरा ।
नामाष्टकार्चनान्तं च कृत्वा तमभिमन्त्रयेत् ॥
6.18.m: Having offered milk-rice and betel and other things as before, / and ending with the worship of the eight names, he should consecrate that [pot] with mantras:

6.18.s:
praṇavāṣṭottaraśataṃ brahmabhiḥ pañcabhiḥ kramāt |
sadyādīśāntamapyastraṃ rakṣitaṃ varmaṇā punaḥ ||
6.18.d:
प्रणवाष्टोत्तरशतं ब्रह्मभिः पञ्चभिः क्रमात् ।
सद्यादीशान्तमप्यस्त्रं रक्षितं वर्मणा पुनः ॥
6.18.m: One hundred and eight times with the Praṇava, and in order with the five Brahman mantras, / from Sadyojāta to Īśāna; then protected by the Astra mantra, [and veiled] with the Kavaca mantra,

6.18.s:
avaguṇṭhya pradarśyātha dhūpadīpau ca bhaktitaḥ |
dhenuyonyākhyamudre ca samyak tatra pradarśayet ||
6.18.d:
अवगुण्ठ्य प्रदर्श्याथ धूपदीपौ च भक्तितः ।
धेनुयोन्याख्यमुद्रे च सम्यक् तत्र प्रदर्शयेत् ॥
6.18.m: having veiled it and displayed incense and lamp with devotion, / he should properly display the gestures called the Dhenu and the Yoni.

6.18.s:
tataśca deśikastasya darbhairācchādya mastakam |
maṇḍalastheśadigbhāge caturasraṃ prakalpayet ||
6.18.d:
ततश्च देशिकस्तस्य दर्भैराच्छाद्य मस्तकम् ।
मण्डलस्थेशदिग्भागे चतुरस्रं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥
6.18.m: Then the teacher, having covered the disciple's head with darbha grass, / should prepare a square in the northeast direction of the maṇḍala.

6.18.s:
taduparyāsanaṃ ramyaṃ kalpayitvā vidhānataḥ |
tatra saṃsthāpayecchiṣyaṃ taṃ śiśuṃ sānukūlataḥ ||
6.18.d:
तदुपर्यासनं रम्यं कल्पयित्वा विधानतः ।
तत्र संस्थापयेच्छिष्यं तं शिशुं सानुकूलतः ॥
6.18.m: Having arranged a delightful seat upon it according to the rule, / he should favorably place that young disciple there.

6.18.s:
tataḥ kumbhaṃ samutthāpya svastivācanapūrvakam |
abhiṣiñced guruḥ śiṣyaṃ prādakṣiṇyena mastake ||
6.18.d:
ततः कुम्भं समुत्थाप्य स्वस्तिवाचनपूर्वकम् ।
अभिषिञ्चेद् गुरुः शिष्यं प्रादक्षिण्येन मस्तके ॥
6.18.m: Then lifting the pot, after reciting the Svasti mantras, / the guru should consecrate the disciple on the head in a clockwise manner.

6.18.s:
praṇavaṃ pūrvamuccārya saptadhā brahmabhistataḥ |
pañcabhiścābhiṣekānte śaṅkhodenābhiveṣṭayet ||
6.18.d:
प्रणवं पूर्वमुच्चार्य सप्तधा ब्रह्मभिस्ततः ।
पञ्चभिश्चाभिषेकान्ते शङ्खोदेनाभिवेष्टयेत् ॥
6.18.m: Having first uttered the Praṇava seven times, then with the five Brahman mantras, / at the end of the consecration he should sprinkle him all around with water from the conch.

6.18.s:
cārudīpaṃ pradarśyātha vāsasā parimṛjya ca |
nūtanaṃ dorakaupīnaṃ vāsasī paridhāpayet ||
6.18.d:
चारुदीपं प्रदर्श्याथ वाससा परिमृज्य च ।
नूतनं दोरकौपीनं वाससी परिधापयेत् ॥
6.18.m: Then, having shown a lovely lamp and wiped him dry with a cloth, / he should clothe him in a new waist-cord, a loincloth, and two garments.

6.18.s:
kṣālitāṅghrirdvirācamya dhṛtabhasmaguruḥ śiśum |
hastābhyāmavalambyātha hastau maṇḍapamadhyataḥ ||
tadaṅgeṣu samālipya tadbhasma vidhinā guruḥ |
āsane sampraveśyātha kalpite sthāpayetsukham ||
6.18.d:
क्षालिताङ्घ्रिर्द्विराचम्य धृतभस्मगुरुः शिशुम् ।
हस्ताभ्यामवलम्ब्याथ हस्तौ मण्डपमध्यतः ॥
तदङ्गेषु समालिप्य तद्भस्म विधिना गुरुः ।
आसने सम्प्रवेश्याथ कल्पिते स्थापयेत्सुखम् ॥
6.18.m:
His feet washed, having sipped water twice, the guru, bearing ash, / holding the youth's hands with both hands from the middle of the pavilion,

and having properly smeared that ash over his limbs, / the guru should then lead him onto the prepared seat and have him sit comfortably.

6.18.s:
pūrvābhimukhamātmīyatattvajñānābhilāṣiṇam |
svāsanastho gururbrūyādamalātmā bhaveti tam ||
6.18.d:
पूर्वाभिमुखमात्मीयतत्त्वज्ञानाभिलाषिणम् ।
स्वासनस्थो गुरुर्ब्रूयादमलात्मा भवेति तम् ॥
6.18.m: To him facing east, desiring the knowledge of his own true reality, / the guru, seated on his own seat with a purified self, should say: “Be of pure self.”

6.18.s:
guruśca paripūrṇo'smi śiva ityacalasthitiḥ |
samādhimācaretsamyaṅ muhūrttaṃ gūḍhamānasaḥ ||
6.18.d:
गुरुश्च परिपूर्णोऽस्मि शिव इत्यचलस्थितिः ।
समाधिमाचरेत्सम्यङ् मुहूर्त्तं गूढमानसः ॥
6.18.m: And the guru, steadfast in the thought “I am Śiva, complete,” / with his mind deep [in contemplation], should properly enter samādhi for a muhūrta.

6.18.s:
paścādunmīlya nayane sānukūlena cetasā |
sāñjaliṃ saṃsthitaṃ śuddhaṃ paśyecchiṣyamanākulaḥ ||
6.18.d:
पश्चादुन्मील्य नयने सानुकूलेन चेतसा ।
साञ्जलिं संस्थितं शुद्धं पश्येच्छिष्यमनाकुलः ॥
6.18.m: Afterward, opening his eyes with a favorable mind, / calm, he should look upon the pure disciple standing with folded hands.

6.18.s:
svahastaṃ bhasitāliptaṃ vinyasya śiśumastake |
dakṣaśrutāvupadiśeddhaṃsaḥ so'hamiti sphuṭam ||
6.18.d:
स्वहस्तं भसितालिप्तं विन्यस्य शिशुमस्तके ।
दक्षश्रुतावुपदिशेद्धंसः सोऽहमिति स्फुटम् ॥
6.18.m: Placing his hand smeared with sacred ash on the youth's head, / he should clearly instruct into his right ear: “Haṃsaḥ, I am He.”

6.18.s:
tatrādyahampadasyārthaḥ śaktyātmā sa śivaḥ svayam |
sa evāhaṃ śivo'smīti svātmānaṃ saṃvibhāvaya ||
6.18.d:
तत्राद्यहम्पदस्यार्थः शक्त्यात्मा स शिवः स्वयम् ।
स एवाहं शिवोऽस्मीति स्वात्मानं संविभावय ॥
6.18.m: Here the meaning of the initial word “aham” is Śiva himself, whose nature is Śakti: / Meditate upon yourself, thinking, “I am indeed that Śiva.”

6.18.s:
ya ityaṇorarthatattvamupadiśya tato vadet |
avāntarāṇāṃ vākyānāmarthatātparyamādarāt ||
6.18.d:
य इत्यणोरर्थतत्त्वमुपदिश्य ततो वदेत् ।
अवान्तराणां वाक्यानामर्थतात्पर्यमादरात् ॥
6.18.m: Having instructed the true meaning of the subtle mantra “yaḥ”, he should then speak / with respect of the meaning and purport of the secondary statements:

6.18.s:
vākyāni vacmi te brahmansāvadhānamatiḥ śṛṇu |
tāni dhāraya citte hi sa brūyāditi saṃsphuṭam ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
oṃ namaḥ śivāya ||
ṣaṣṭhī kailāsasaṃhitā
6.18.d:
वाक्यानि वच्मि ते ब्रह्मन्सावधानमतिः शृणु ।
तानि धारय चित्ते हि स ब्रूयादिति संस्फुटम् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
ओं नमः शिवाय ॥
षष्ठी कैलाससंहिता
6.18.m:
“I shall speak these statements to you, O Brahmin; listen with an attentive mind! / Indeed, hold them in your heart”; thus he should clearly say.

Homage to the holy Gaurī and Śaṅkara.

The Sixth, Kailāsasaṃhitā.

6.19.s:
subrahmaṇya uvāca |
atha mahāvākyāni prajñānaṃ brahma ||
6.19.d:
सुब्रह्मण्य उवाच ।
अथ महावाक्यानि प्रज्ञानं ब्रह्म ॥
6.19.m: Subrahmaṇya said: / Now the Great Sayings: “Brahman is consciousness.”
“What is here is there, what is there is here.”
“It is other than the known and above the unknown.”
“This is our immortal inner controller, the self.”

6.19.s: sa yaścāyaṃ puruṣe yaścāsāvāditye sa ekaḥ ||
6.19.d: स यश्चायं पुरुषे यश्चासावादित्ये स एकः ॥
6.19.m: “He who is this person here and he who is that in the sun, he is one.”
“I am supreme Brahman, beyond the higher and the lower, higher than the highest.”
“By virtue of the Vedas and śāstras, and of the guru, I am of the nature of bliss itself.”
“The Brahman residing in all beings is that very self which I am; there is no doubt.”
“I am the life of the real; I am the life of the earth.”
“I am the life of the waters; I am the life of fire.”
“I am the life of wind; I am the life of space.”
“I am the life of the three guṇas.”

6.19.s: sarvo'haṃ sarvātmako'haṃ saṃsārī yadbhūtaṃ yacca bhavyaṃ yadvartamānaṃ sarvātmakatvādadvitīyo'ham ||
6.19.d: सर्वोऽहं सर्वात्मकोऽहं संसारी यद्भूतं यच्च भव्यं यद्वर्तमानं सर्वात्मकत्वादद्वितीयोऽहम् ॥
6.19.m: “I am all, I am the self of all, the transmigrating being, whatever was, whatever will be, and whatever is present; because I am the self of all, I am without a second.”
“All this is indeed Brahman.”

6.19.s:
yo'sau so'haṃ haṃsaḥ so'hamasmi |
ityevaṃ sarvatra sadā dhyāyediti | atha mahāvākyānāmarthamāha |
prajñānaṃ brahmavākyārthaḥ pūrvameva prabodhitaḥ |
ahampadasyārthabhūtaḥ śaktyātmā parameśvaraḥ | 1|
akāraḥ sarvavarṇāgryaḥ prakāśaḥ paramaḥ śivaḥ |
hakāro vyomarūpaḥ syācchaktyātmā samprakīrtitaḥ | 2|
śivaśaktyostu saṃyogādānandaḥ satatoditaḥ |
brahmeti śivaśaktyostu sarvātmatvamiti sphuṭam | 3|
pūrvamevopadiṣṭaṃ tatso'hamasmīti bhāvayet |
tattvamityatra taditi tacchabdārthaḥ prabodhitaḥ | 4|
anyathā so'hamityatra viparītārthabhāvanā |
ahaṃśabdastu puruṣastaditi syānnapuṃsakam |
evamanyo'nyavairudhyādanvayo na bhavettayoḥ | 5|
strīpuṃrūpasya jagataḥ kāraṇaṃ cānyathā bhavet |
sa tattvamasi ityevamupadeśārthabhāvanā | 6|
6.19.d:
योऽसौ सोऽहं हंसः सोऽहमस्मि ।
इत्येवं सर्वत्र सदा ध्यायेदिति । अथ महावाक्यानामर्थमाह ।
प्रज्ञानं ब्रह्मवाक्यार्थः पूर्वमेव प्रबोधितः ।
अहम्पदस्यार्थभूतः शक्त्यात्मा परमेश्वरः । 1।
अकारः सर्ववर्णाग्र्यः प्रकाशः परमः शिवः ।
हकारो व्योमरूपः स्याच्छक्त्यात्मा सम्प्रकीर्तितः । 2।
शिवशक्त्योस्तु संयोगादानन्दः सततोदितः ।
ब्रह्मेति शिवशक्त्योस्तु सर्वात्मत्वमिति स्फुटम् । 3।
पूर्वमेवोपदिष्टं तत्सोऽहमस्मीति भावयेत् ।
तत्त्वमित्यत्र तदिति तच्छब्दार्थः प्रबोधितः । 4।
अन्यथा सोऽहमित्यत्र विपरीतार्थभावना ।
अहंशब्दस्तु पुरुषस्तदिति स्यान्नपुंसकम् ।
एवमन्योऽन्यवैरुध्यादन्वयो न भवेत्तयोः । 5।
स्त्रीपुंरूपस्य जगतः कारणं चान्यथा भवेत् ।
स तत्त्वमसि इत्येवमुपदेशार्थभावना । 6।
6.19.m:
“He who is that, I am he; Haṃsa, I am he.” / Thus one should always meditate everywhere. Now he explains the meaning of the Great Sayings: / The meaning of the sentence “Brahman is consciousness” was already taught earlier. / Parameśvara, whose essence is Śakti, is the true referent of the word “aham”. 1.

The letter “a”, foremost of all letters, is manifestation, the Supreme Śiva; / the letter “ha” is the form of space, proclaimed as having the nature of Śakti. 2.

From the union of Śiva and Śakti, bliss is eternally arisen; / “Brahman” is clearly the state of being the self of all of both Śiva and Śakti. 3.

That was already taught earlier; one should meditate: “I am He.” / In “tattvam” [you are that], by “tat” the meaning of the word “tat” is explained. 4.

Otherwise, in “so'ham” [I am He], there would be an apprehension of an incongruous sense: / the word “aham” is masculine, while “tat” is neuter; / thus, due to mutual contradiction, there would be no syntactical connection between them. 5.

And the cause of the world, which has male and female forms, would be otherwise; / such is the apprehension of the meaning of the instruction “He, you are that.” 6.

6.19.s:
ayamātmeti vākye ca puṃrūpaṃ padayugmakam |
īśena rakṣaṇīyatvādīśāvāsyamidaṃ jagat | 7|
prajñānātmā yadeveha tadamutreti cintayet |
yaḥ sa eveti vidvadbhiḥ siddhāntibhirihocyate | 8|
uparisthitavākye ca yo'mutra sa iha sthitaḥ |
iti pūrvavadevārthaḥ puruṣo viduṣāṃ mataḥ | 9|
anyadeva tadviditādatho aviditādapi |
asminvākye phalasyāpi vaiparītyavibhāvanā | 6.19.10|
yathā syāttadvadevātra vakṣyāmi śrūyatāṃ mune |
ayathāviditāśabdo pūrvavadviditāditi | 11|
pravṛttaḥ syāttadviditāttathaivāviditātparam |
anyadeva hi saṃsiddhyai na bhavediti niścitam | 12|
eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmī yo'mṛtaśca śivaḥ svayam |
yaścāyaṃ puruṣe śambhuryaścāditye vyavasthitaḥ | 13|
sa cā'sau seti pārthakyaṃ naikaṃ sarvaṃ sa īritaḥ |
sopādhidvayamasyārtha upacārāttathocyate | 14|
6.19.d:
अयमात्मेति वाक्ये च पुंरूपं पदयुग्मकम् ।
ईशेन रक्षणीयत्वादीशावास्यमिदं जगत् । 7।
प्रज्ञानात्मा यदेवेह तदमुत्रेति चिन्तयेत् ।
यः स एवेति विद्वद्भिः सिद्धान्तिभिरिहोच्यते । 8।
उपरिस्थितवाक्ये च योऽमुत्र स इह स्थितः ।
इति पूर्ववदेवार्थः पुरुषो विदुषां मतः । 9।
अन्यदेव तद्विदितादथो अविदितादपि ।
अस्मिन्वाक्ये फलस्यापि वैपरीत्यविभावना । 6.19.10।
यथा स्यात्तद्वदेवात्र वक्ष्यामि श्रूयतां मुने ।
अयथाविदिताशब्दो पूर्ववद्विदितादिति । 11।
प्रवृत्तः स्यात्तद्विदितात्तथैवाविदितात्परम् ।
अन्यदेव हि संसिद्ध्यै न भवेदिति निश्चितम् । 12।
एष त आत्मान्तर्यामी योऽमृतश्च शिवः स्वयम् ।
यश्चायं पुरुषे शम्भुर्यश्चादित्ये व्यवस्थितः । 13।
स चाऽसौ सेति पार्थक्यं नैकं सर्वं स ईरितः ।
सोपाधिद्वयमस्यार्थ उपचारात्तथोच्यते । 14।
6.19.m:
And in the sentence “This self”, the pair of words has a masculine form; / because it is to be protected by the Lord, “this world is to be enveloped by the Lord.” 7.

One should contemplate: “The self of consciousness, whatever is here, that is there”; / “He who is that is the very same,” so it is said here by the wise Siddhāntins. 8.

And in the following sentence, “He who is there, he dwells here”; / thus the meaning is just as before, understood as the Person by the wise. 9.

“Other indeed than the known, and also above the unknown” — / in this sentence, there is also the apprehension of the inverted fruit. 10.

Just as it is, so I shall speak of it here; let it be heard, O sage: / the word “aviditāt” [from the unknown], like the preceding “viditāt” [from the known], 11.

would apply: “beyond the known and likewise beyond the unknown, / [it is] other indeed”; for it cannot fail to lead to complete attainment; this is certain. 12.

“This is your self, the inner controller, who is immortal,” is Śiva himself; / and Śambhu is he who is in the person, and he who resides in the sun. 13.

And 'he is that, she is that'—this differentiation is not one; he is declared to be everything. / The sense of his having two adjuncts is stated in that manner metaphorically. | 14

6.19.s:
taṃ śambhunāthaṃ śrutayo vadanti hi hiraṇmayam |
hiraṇyabāhava iti sarvāṅgasyopalakṣalam | 15|
anyathā tatpatitvaṃ tu na bhavediti yatnataḥ |
ya eṣo'ntariti śambhuśchāndogye śrūyate śivaḥ | 16|
hiraṇyaśmaśruvāṃstadvaddhiraṇyamayakeśavān |
nakhamārabhya keśāntaṃ sarvatrāpi hiraṇmayaḥ | 17|
ahamasmi paraṃ brahma parāparaparātparam |
iti vākyasya tātparyaṃ vadāmi śrūyatāmidam | 18|
ahampadasyārthabhūtaḥ śaktyātmā śiva īritaḥ |
sa evāsmīti vākyārtha yojanā bhavati dhruvam | 19|
sarvotkṛṣṭaśca sarvātmā parabrahma sa īritaḥ |
paraścāthāparaśceti parātparamiti tridhā | 6.19.20|
rudro brahmā ca viṣṇuśca proktāḥ śrutyaiva nānyathā |
tebhyaśca paramo devaḥ paraśabdena bodhitaḥ | 21|
vedaśāstragurūṇāṃ ca vākyābhyāsavaśācchiśoḥ |
pūrṇānandamayaḥ śambhuḥ prādurbhūto bhaveddhṛdi | 22|
6.19.d:
तं शम्भुनाथं श्रुतयो वदन्ति हि हिरण्मयम् ।
हिरण्यबाहव इति सर्वाङ्गस्योपलक्षलम् । 15।
अन्यथा तत्पतित्वं तु न भवेदिति यत्नतः ।
य एषोऽन्तरिति शम्भुश्छान्दोग्ये श्रूयते शिवः । 16।
हिरण्यश्मश्रुवांस्तद्वद्धिरण्यमयकेशवान् ।
नखमारभ्य केशान्तं सर्वत्रापि हिरण्मयः । 17।
अहमस्मि परं ब्रह्म परापरपरात्परम् ।
इति वाक्यस्य तात्पर्यं वदामि श्रूयतामिदम् । 18।
अहम्पदस्यार्थभूतः शक्त्यात्मा शिव ईरितः ।
स एवास्मीति वाक्यार्थ योजना भवति ध्रुवम् । 19।
सर्वोत्कृष्टश्च सर्वात्मा परब्रह्म स ईरितः ।
परश्चाथापरश्चेति परात्परमिति त्रिधा । 6.19.20।
रुद्रो ब्रह्मा च विष्णुश्च प्रोक्ताः श्रुत्यैव नान्यथा ।
तेभ्यश्च परमो देवः परशब्देन बोधितः । 21।
वेदशास्त्रगुरूणां च वाक्याभ्यासवशाच्छिशोः ।
पूर्णानन्दमयः शम्भुः प्रादुर्भूतो भवेद्धृदि । 22।
6.19.m:
Indeed, the Vedic texts declare that lord Śambhu to be golden: / the expression 'with golden arms' indicates his whole body. | 15

Otherwise, his rulership over that could not be; hence diligently / Śambhu, who is Śiva, is heard in the Chāndogya [Upaniṣad as] 'he who is within'. | 16

Likewise, he has a golden beard and golden hair; / beginning from the nails to the tips of the hair, he is golden everywhere. | 17

'I am the supreme Brahman, higher than the high and the low'— / listen to this as I explain the purport of this statement: | 18

Śiva, who is identical with Śakti, is declared to be the referent of the word 'I'; / 'I am that very one'—this is certainly the syntactic construal of the sentence. | 19

And supreme above all, the self of all, he is declared to be the supreme Brahman. / 'Higher', 'lower', and 'higher than the high'—thus threefold | 20

Rudra, Brahmā, and Viṣṇu are indeed declared by the Veda, and not otherwise; / and the god supreme beyond them is denoted by the word 'higher'. | 21

By virtue of the child's practice of the words of the Vedas, scriptures, and gurus, / Śambhu, full of complete bliss, becomes manifest in the heart: | 22

6.19.s:
sarvabhūtasthitaḥ śambhuḥ sa evāhaṃ na saṃśayaḥ |
tattvajātasya sarvasya prāṇo'smyahamahaṃ śivaḥ | 23|
ityuktvā punarapyāha śivastattvatrayasya ca |
prāṇo'smītyatra pṛthvyādiguṇāntagrahaṇānmune | 24|
ātmatattvāni sarvāṇi gṛhītānīti bhāvaya |
punaśca sarvagrahaṇaṃ vidyātattve śivātmanoḥ | 25|
tattvayoścāsmyahaṃ prāṇāḥ sarvaḥ sarvātmako hyaham |
jīvasya cāntaryāmitvājjīvo'haṃ tasya sarvadā | 26|
yadbhūtaṃ yacca bhavyaṃ yadbhaviṣyatsarvameva ca |
manmayatvādahaṃ sarvaḥ sarvo vai rudra ityapi | 27|
śrutirāha mune sā hi sākṣācchivamukhodgatā |
sarvātmā paramairebhirguṇairnityasamanvayāt | 28|
svasmātparātmavirahādadvitīyo'hameva hi |
sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahmeti vākyārthaḥ pūrvamīritaḥ | 29|
pūrṇo'haṃ bhāvarūpatvānnityamukto'hameva hi |
paśavo matprasādena muktā madbhāvamāśritāḥ | 6.19.30|
6.19.d:
सर्वभूतस्थितः शम्भुः स एवाहं न संशयः ।
तत्त्वजातस्य सर्वस्य प्राणोऽस्म्यहमहं शिवः । 23।
इत्युक्त्वा पुनरप्याह शिवस्तत्त्वत्रयस्य च ।
प्राणोऽस्मीत्यत्र पृथ्व्यादिगुणान्तग्रहणान्मुने । 24।
आत्मतत्त्वानि सर्वाणि गृहीतानीति भावय ।
पुनश्च सर्वग्रहणं विद्यातत्त्वे शिवात्मनोः । 25।
तत्त्वयोश्चास्म्यहं प्राणाः सर्वः सर्वात्मको ह्यहम् ।
जीवस्य चान्तर्यामित्वाज्जीवोऽहं तस्य सर्वदा । 26।
यद्भूतं यच्च भव्यं यद्भविष्यत्सर्वमेव च ।
मन्मयत्वादहं सर्वः सर्वो वै रुद्र इत्यपि । 27।
श्रुतिराह मुने सा हि साक्षाच्छिवमुखोद्गता ।
सर्वात्मा परमैरेभिर्गुणैर्नित्यसमन्वयात् । 28।
स्वस्मात्परात्मविरहादद्वितीयोऽहमेव हि ।
सर्वं खल्विदं ब्रह्मेति वाक्यार्थः पूर्वमीरितः । 29।
पूर्णोऽहं भावरूपत्वान्नित्यमुक्तोऽहमेव हि ।
पशवो मत्प्रसादेन मुक्ता मद्भावमाश्रिताः । 6.19.30।
6.19.m:
'Śambhu dwells in all beings; I am indeed he, there is no doubt. / I am the vital breath of the entire collection of principles; I am Śiva.' | 23

Having said this, Śiva spoke again: 'And of the three principles, / I am the vital breath'—here, O sage, by taking [them] up to the qualities beginning with earth, | 24

understand that all the self-principles (ātmatattva) have been included. / And further, the inclusion of all in the principle of knowledge (vidyātattva) and of Śiva: | 25

'I am the vital breath of both principles; indeed, I am all, comprising all. / And because of being the inner controller of the individual soul, I am always that soul. | 26

Whatever has been, whatever is present, and whatever will be—all that, / because it consists of me, I am all, and all is indeed Rudra.' | 27

Thus the Vedic text says, O sage, having arisen directly from the mouth of Śiva: / 'Because of eternal association with these supreme qualities, I am the self of all. | 28

Because of the absence of any supreme self apart from myself, I alone am without a second.' / The meaning of the statement 'All this is indeed Brahman' was stated previously. | 29

'I am full, because my nature is pure being; I alone am eternally free. / By my grace the bound souls are liberated, having taken refuge in my state of being.' | 30

6.19.s:
yo'sau sarvātmakaḥ śambhuḥ so'haṃ haṃsa śivo'smyaham |
iti vai sarvavākyārtho vāmadeva śivoditaḥ | 31|
itīśaśrutivākyābhvāmupadiṣṭārthamādarāt |
sākṣācchivaikyadaṃ puṃsāṃ śiśorgururupādiśet | 32|
ādāya śaṅkhaṃ sādhāramastramantreṇa bhasmanā |
śodhya tatpurataḥ sthāpya caturasre samarcite | 33|
omityabhyarcya gandhādyairastraṃ vastropaśobhitam |
vāsitaṃ jalamāpūrya sampūjyomiti mantrataḥ | 34|
saptadhaivābhimantryātha praṇavena punaśca tam |
yastvantaraṃ kiñcidapi kurute so'tibhītibhāk | 35|
ityāha śrutisattattvaṃ dṛḍhātmā gatabhīrbhava |
ityābhāṣya svayaṃ śiṣyaṃ devaṃ dhyāyan samarcayet | 36|
śiṣyāsanaṃ samprapūjya ṣaḍutthāpanamārgataḥ |
śivāsanaṃ ca saṅkalpya śivamūrtiṃ prakalpayet | 37|
pañca brahmāṇi vinyasya śiraḥ pādāvasānakam |
muṇḍavaktrakalābhedaiḥ praṇavasya kalā api | 38|
6.19.d:
योऽसौ सर्वात्मकः शम्भुः सोऽहं हंस शिवोऽस्म्यहम् ।
इति वै सर्ववाक्यार्थो वामदेव शिवोदितः । 31।
इतीशश्रुतिवाक्याभ्वामुपदिष्टार्थमादरात् ।
साक्षाच्छिवैक्यदं पुंसां शिशोर्गुरुरुपादिशेत् । 32।
आदाय शङ्खं साधारमस्त्रमन्त्रेण भस्मना ।
शोध्य तत्पुरतः स्थाप्य चतुरस्रे समर्चिते । 33।
ओमित्यभ्यर्च्य गन्धाद्यैरस्त्रं वस्त्रोपशोभितम् ।
वासितं जलमापूर्य सम्पूज्योमिति मन्त्रतः । 34।
सप्तधैवाभिमन्त्र्याथ प्रणवेन पुनश्च तम् ।
यस्त्वन्तरं किञ्चिदपि कुरुते सोऽतिभीतिभाक् । 35।
इत्याह श्रुतिसत्तत्त्वं दृढात्मा गतभीर्भव ।
इत्याभाष्य स्वयं शिष्यं देवं ध्यायन् समर्चयेत् । 36।
शिष्यासनं सम्प्रपूज्य षडुत्थापनमार्गतः ।
शिवासनं च सङ्कल्प्य शिवमूर्तिं प्रकल्पयेत् । 37।
पञ्च ब्रह्माणि विन्यस्य शिरः पादावसानकम् ।
मुण्डवक्त्रकलाभेदैः प्रणवस्य कला अपि । 38।
6.19.m:
'That Śambhu who comprises all, that I am; Haṃsa, I am Śiva.' / This indeed is the meaning of all statements, O Vāmadeva, spoken by Śiva. | 31

The guru should respectfully teach the child this meaning taught / by both the statements of Īśa and the Vedas, which bestows direct union with Śiva upon persons. | 32

Taking a conch along with its base, purifying it with the Astra mantra / and with ashes, placing it in front upon a square that has been worshipped, | 33

worshipping the weapon adorned with cloth with perfumes and other offerings with 'Om', / filling it with scented water, worshipping it with the mantra 'Om', | 34

and consecrating it seven times with the praṇava, / and then [saying]: 'He who makes even the slightest differentiation incurs great fear'— | 35

thus the Vedic text states the true reality; be firm in self and free from fear.' / Having spoken thus to the disciple himself, he should worship while meditating on the god. | 36

Having worshipped the disciple's seat according to the method of the sixfold installation, / and having conceptualized the seat of Śiva, he should conceptualize the form of Śiva. | 37

Having installed the five Brahmā mantras, from the head down to the feet, / by dividing the parts of the head and faces, and also the parts of the praṇava | 38

6.19.s:
aṣṭatriṃśanmantrarūpāḥ śiṣyadehe'tha mastake |
samāvāhya śivaṃ mudrāḥ sthāpanīyāḥ pradarśayet | 39|
tataścāṅgāni vinyasya sarvajñānītyanukramāt |
kalpayedupacārāṃśca ṣoḍaśāsanapūrvakām | 6.19.40|
pāyasānnaṃ ca naivedyaṃ samarpyomagnijāyayā |
gaṇḍūṣācamanārghyādi dhūpadīpādikaṃ kramāt | 41|
nāmāṣṭakena sampūjya brāhmaṇairvedapāragaiḥ |
japed brahmavidāpnoti bhṛgurvai vāruṇistataḥ | 42|
yo devānāmupakramya yaḥ paraḥ sa maheśvaraḥ |
ityantaṃ tasya purataḥ kahlārādivinirmitām | 43|
ādāya mālāmutthāya śrīvirūpākṣanirmite |
śāstre pañcāsyake rūpe siddhiskandhaṃ japecchanaiḥ | 44|
khyātiḥ pūrṇo'hamityantaṃ sānukūlena cetasā |
deśikastasya śiṣyasya kaṇṭhadeśe samarpayet | 45|
tilakaṃ candanenātha sarvāṅgālepanaṃ punaḥ |
svasampradāyānuguṇaṃ kārayecca yathāvidhi | 46|
6.19.d:
अष्टत्रिंशन्मन्त्ररूपाः शिष्यदेहेऽथ मस्तके ।
समावाह्य शिवं मुद्राः स्थापनीयाः प्रदर्शयेत् । 39।
ततश्चाङ्गानि विन्यस्य सर्वज्ञानीत्यनुक्रमात् ।
कल्पयेदुपचारांश्च षोडशासनपूर्वकाम् । 6.19.40।
पायसान्नं च नैवेद्यं समर्प्योमग्निजायया ।
गण्डूषाचमनार्घ्यादि धूपदीपादिकं क्रमात् । 41।
नामाष्टकेन सम्पूज्य ब्राह्मणैर्वेदपारगैः ।
जपेद् ब्रह्मविदाप्नोति भृगुर्वै वारुणिस्ततः । 42।
यो देवानामुपक्रम्य यः परः स महेश्वरः ।
इत्यन्तं तस्य पुरतः कह्लारादिविनिर्मिताम् । 43।
आदाय मालामुत्थाय श्रीविरूपाक्षनिर्मिते ।
शास्त्रे पञ्चास्यके रूपे सिद्धिस्कन्धं जपेच्छनैः । 44।
ख्यातिः पूर्णोऽहमित्यन्तं सानुकूलेन चेतसा ।
देशिकस्तस्य शिष्यस्य कण्ठदेशे समर्पयेत् । 45।
तिलकं चन्दनेनाथ सर्वाङ्गालेपनं पुनः ।
स्वसम्प्रदायानुगुणं कारयेच्च यथाविधि । 46।
6.19.m:
consisting of thirty-eight mantras on the disciple's body and head, / and having invoked Śiva, he should display the mudrās to be established. | 39

Then, having installed the ancillary mantras in order with 'Sarvajña' and the rest, / he should offer the sixteen services of worship beginning with the seat. | 40

Having offered the food offering of milk-rice with 'Om' and the wife of Agni (Svāhā), / he should perform in order the mouth-rinsing, sipping, water-offering, incense, lamp, and so forth. | 41

Having worshipped with the eight names along with brāhmaṇas who have mastered the Vedas, / he should recite 'The knower of Brahman attains', then 'Bhṛgu, son of Varuṇa', | 42

and beginning with 'He who among the gods' up to 'He who is supreme is Maheśvara'. / In front of him, having taken a garland made of white water-lilies and other flowers, | 43

and having stood up, in the scripture composed by the venerable Virūpākṣa / in the five-faced form, he should slowly recite the chapter on accomplishment, | 44

ending with 'renowned, I am complete'. With a favorable mind, / the preceptor should place [the garland] upon the neck of that disciple. | 45

Then, according to the rule, in conformity with his own tradition, / he should have an auspicious forehead mark made with sandalwood and anointment of the whole body. | 46

6.19.s:
tataśca deśikaḥ prītyā nāma śrīpādasaṃjñitam |
chatraṃ ca pādukāṃ dadyād dūrvākalpavikalpanam | 47|
vyākhyātṛtvaṃ ca karmādi gurvāsanaparigraham |
anugṛhya gurustasmai śiṣyāya śivarūpiṇe | 48|
śivo'hamasmīti sadā samādhistho bhaveti tam |
samprocyātha svayaṃ tasmai namaskāraṃ samācaret | 49|
sampradāyānuguṇyena namaskuryustathāpare |
śiṣyastadā samutthāya namaskuryād guruṃ tathā |
gurorapi guruṃ tasya śiṣyāṃśca svagurorapi | 6.19.50|
evaṃ kṛtanamaskāraṃ śiṣyaṃ dadyād guruḥ svayam |
suśīlaṃ yatavācaṃ taṃ vinayāvanataṃ sthitam | 51|
adya prabhṛti lokānāmanugrahaparo bhava |
parīkṣya vatsaraṃ śiṣyamaṅgīkuru vidhānataḥ | 52|
rāgādidoṣānsantyajya śivadhyānaparo bhava |
satsampradāyasaṃsiddhaiḥ saṅgaṃ kuru na cetaraiḥ | 53|
6.19.d:
ततश्च देशिकः प्रीत्या नाम श्रीपादसंज्ञितम् ।
छत्रं च पादुकां दद्याद् दूर्वाकल्पविकल्पनम् । 47।
व्याख्यातृत्वं च कर्मादि गुर्वासनपरिग्रहम् ।
अनुगृह्य गुरुस्तस्मै शिष्याय शिवरूपिणे । 48।
शिवोऽहमस्मीति सदा समाधिस्थो भवेति तम् ।
सम्प्रोच्याथ स्वयं तस्मै नमस्कारं समाचरेत् । 49।
सम्प्रदायानुगुण्येन नमस्कुर्युस्तथापरे ।
शिष्यस्तदा समुत्थाय नमस्कुर्याद् गुरुं तथा ।
गुरोरपि गुरुं तस्य शिष्यांश्च स्वगुरोरपि । 6.19.50।
एवं कृतनमस्कारं शिष्यं दद्याद् गुरुः स्वयम् ।
सुशीलं यतवाचं तं विनयावनतं स्थितम् । 51।
अद्य प्रभृति लोकानामनुग्रहपरो भव ।
परीक्ष्य वत्सरं शिष्यमङ्गीकुरु विधानतः । 52।
रागादिदोषान्सन्त्यज्य शिवध्यानपरो भव ।
सत्सम्प्रदायसंसिद्धैः सङ्गं कुरु न चेतरैः । 53।
6.19.m:
And then the preceptor, with affection, should give the name designated by 'Śrīpāda', / an umbrella, sandals, and the arrangement of the dūrvā grass rites. | 47

Conferring the authority to expound, rites, and the assumption of the guru's seat, / the guru, having favored that disciple who has the form of Śiva, | 48

and saying to him: 'Always remain in absorption, knowing "I am Śiva"', / should himself bow down to him. | 49

The others should likewise bow down in accordance with tradition. / The disciple should then stand up and bow to the guru, / as well as to the guru of the guru, and to the disciples of his own guru. | 50

The guru himself should instruct the disciple who has thus bowed, / who is of good character, restrained in speech, and standing bowed with modesty: | 51

'From this day forward, be devoted to showing favor to the worlds. / Having tested a disciple for a year, accept him according to the rules. | 52

Abandoning faults such as passion, be devoted to meditation on Śiva. / Associate with those perfected in the true tradition, and not with others. | 53

6.19.s:
anabhyarcya śivaṃ jātu mā bhuṅkṣvāprāṇa saṅkṣayam |
gurubhaktiṃ samāsthāya sukhī bhava sukhī bhava | 54|
iti kramād guruvaro dayālurjñānasāgaraḥ |
sānukūlena cittena samaṃ śiṣyaṃ samācaret | 55|
tava snehānmayāyaṃ vai vāmadeva munīśvara |
yogapaṭṭaprakāraste prokto guhyataro'pi hi | 56|
ityuktvā ṣaṇmukhastasmai kṣaurasnānavidhikramam |
vaktumārabhate prītyā yatīnāṃ kṛpayā śubham | 57|
6.19.d:
अनभ्यर्च्य शिवं जातु मा भुङ्क्ष्वाप्राण सङ्क्षयम् ।
गुरुभक्तिं समास्थाय सुखी भव सुखी भव । 54।
इति क्रमाद् गुरुवरो दयालुर्ज्ञानसागरः ।
सानुकूलेन चित्तेन समं शिष्यं समाचरेत् । 55।
तव स्नेहान्मयायं वै वामदेव मुनीश्वर ।
योगपट्टप्रकारस्ते प्रोक्तो गुह्यतरोऽपि हि । 56।
इत्युक्त्वा षण्मुखस्तस्मै क्षौरस्नानविधिक्रमम् ।
वक्तुमारभते प्रीत्या यतीनां कृपया शुभम् । 57।
6.19.m:
Never eat without having worshipped Śiva, until the end of your life. / Devoted to the guru, be happy, be happy!' | 54

In this manner, the excellent guru, compassionate, an ocean of knowledge, / should treat the disciple as an equal with a favorable mind. | 55

'Out of affection for you, O Vāmadeva, lord of sages, / this method of the yogapaṭṭa, exceedingly secret though it is, has been declared by me.' | 56

Having said this, Ṣaṇmukha, out of grace and with affection, began / to state for him the auspicious procedure for shaving and bathing of ascetics. | 57

6.19.s: iti śrīśivamahāpurāṇe ṣaṣṭhyāṃ kailāsasaṃhitāyāṃ yogapaṭṭavidhivarṇanaṃ nāmaikonaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ | 6.19|
6.19.d: इति श्रीशिवमहापुराणे षष्ठ्यां कैलाससंहितायां योगपट्टविधिवर्णनं नामैकोनविंशोऽध्यायः । 6.19।
6.19.m: Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Procedure for the Yogapaṭṭa', in the Kailāsasaṃhitā, the sixth [book] of the glorious Śivamahāpurāṇa. | 6.19

6.19.s:
6.20 | śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ | | śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ | | śrīśivamahāpurāṇam | | oṃ namaḥ śivāya |
ṣaṣṭhī kailāsasaṃhitā
6.19.d:
6.20 । श्रीगणेशाय नमः । । श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः । । श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् । । ओं नमः शिवाय ।
षष्ठी कैलाससंहिता
6.19.m:
6.20 | Homage to holy Gaṇeśa! | Homage to holy Gaurī and Śaṅkara! | The holy Śivamahāpurāṇa | Oṃ homage to Śiva!
Sixth Kailāsasaṃhitā.

6.19.s:
subrahmaṇya uvāca |
kṣaurasnānavidhiṃ vakṣye vāmadeva mahāmune |
yasya sadyo vidhānena śuddhiḥ syādyatinaḥ parā | 1|
yogapaṭṭaprakārasya vidhiṃ prāpya munīśvara |
sa śiṣyaḥ syād vratī pūrṇaḥ kṣaurakarmodyato bhavet | 2|
guruṃ natvā viśeṣeṇa labdhānujñastato guroḥ |
śiraḥ saṅkṣālya cācamya savāsāḥ kṣauramācaret | 3|
kṣālayedvasanaṃ paścānmṛdambhobhiḥ kṣurādikam |
taddhastau ca mṛdālipya kṣālayeti mṛdaṃ dadet | 4|
sthāpitaṃ prokṣitaṃ toyaiḥ śivaṃ śivamitīrayan |
svanetre pihite caivānāmāṅguṣṭhābhimantrite | 5|
astreṇonmīlya sandṛśya kṣurādikṣaurasādhanam |
abhimantrya dvādaśātha prokṣayedastramantrataḥ | 6|
kṣuraṃ gṛhītvā tāreṇa dakṣabhāge nikṛntayet |
keśāṃśca kāṃścidagreṣu vaptvā sarvaṃ ca vāpayet | 7|
pṛthivyāṃ parṇamādāya vikṣipenna bhuvaḥ sthale |
śmaśrūṇi hastapādasthanakhāni ca nikṛntayet | 8|
bilvāśvatthatulasyādisthāne saṅgṛhya mṛttikām |
dviṣaḍvāraṃ nimajyāpsu tīraṃ gatvopaviśya ca | 9|
śuddhe deśe tu saṃsthāpya mṛdaṃ tredhā vibhajya ca |
evaṃ punastridhā kṛtvā prokṣyāstreṇābhimantrayet | 6.20.10|
tatraikāṃ mṛdamādāya dāpayitvānyapāṇinā |
karau dvādaśadhālipya pratyekaṃ kena kṣālayet | 11|
punarekāṃ pādayośca mukhe cānyāṃ kare kramāt |
saṃlipyākṣālya cāmbhobhiḥ punaśca jalamāviśet | 12|
anyāṃ mṛdaṃ bhāgayitvā śirasi dvādaśa kramāt |
ālipya mṛdamāsyāntaṃ nimajya ca punaḥ punaḥ | 13|
tīraṃ gatvā tu gaṇḍūṣān ṣoḍaśācamanaṃ dvidhā |
prāṇānāyamya ca punaḥ praṇavaṃ dvyaṣṭasaṅkhyayā | 14|
mṛdamanyāṃ punastredhā vibhajya ca tadekayā |
kaṭiśaucaṃ pādaśaucaṃ vidhāyācamya ca dvidhā | 15|
praṇavenātha ṣoḍaśa prāṇānāyamya vāgyataḥ |
punaranyāṃ svorudeśe tridhā vinyasya comiti | 16|
prokṣyābhimantrayetsapta svapāṇyostalamekadhā |
tridhālipyātha sampaśyetsūryamūrtiṃ ca pāvanīm | 17|
svakakṣayoḥ samālipya vyatyastābhyāmathānyayā |
pāṇibhyāṃ ca mṛdā śiṣyaḥ sumatirdṛḍhamānasaḥ | 18|
gṛhītvānyāṃ mṛdaṃ śuddhāṃ tathāsau gurubhaktimān |
śira ārabhya pādāntaṃ vilipyādityadṛṣṭayā | 19|
samutthāya tato'sau vai daṇḍamādāya bhūtale |
svaguruṃ mantradaṃ bhaktyā saṃsmarejjñānaniṣṭhayā | 6.20.20|
tataḥ sāmbaṃ maheśānaṃ śaṅkaraṃ candraśekharam |
saṃsmaredbhaktitaḥ śiṣya sarvaiśvaryapatiṃ śivam | 21|
trivāraṃ praṇametprītyā sāṣṭāṅgaṃ ca guruṃ śivam |
pañcāṅgenaikavāraṃ ca samutthāya ca vandayet | 22|
tīrthaṃ praviśya tanmadhye nimajyonmajya tāṃ mṛdam |
skandhe saṃsthāpya pūrvoktaprakāreṇa vilepayet | 23|
tatrāvaśiṣṭaṃ saṅgṛhya jalamadhye praviśya ca |
viloḍya samyak tāṃ tatra sarvāṅgeṣu vilipya ca | 24|
trivāramomiti procya śivapādāmbujaṃ smaran |
saṃsārāmbudhisantāraṃ sadā yadvidhito hi saḥ | 25|
abhiṣicyomiti jalaṃ virajābhasmalolitam |
aṅgopamārjjanaṃ kṛtvā susnāyādbhasmanā tataḥ | 26|
tripuṇḍraṃ ca vidhāyātha yathoktavidhinā śubham |
yathoktāṅgeṣu sarveṣu sāvadhānatayā mune | 27|
tataḥ śuddhamanā bhūtvā kuryānmadhyadinakriyāḥ |
maheśvaraṃ namaskṛtya gurūṃstīrthādikāni ca | 28|
sampūjayenmaheśānaṃ bhaktyā paramayā mune |
sāmbikaṃ jñānadātāraṃ pātāraṃ tribhavasya vai | 29|
tato'sau dṛḍhacetasko yatiḥ svavṛṣasaṃsthitaḥ |
bhikṣārthaṃ pravrajecchuddho vipravargeṣu sādhuṣu | 6.20.30|
tatastatra ca śuddhātmā pañcadhā parikalpitam |
bhaikṣyaṃ yathocitaṃ kuryād dūṣitānnaṃ vivarjayet | 31|
śaucaṃ snānaṃ tathā bhikṣāṃ nityamekāntasevanam |
bhikṣauścatvāri karmāṇi pañcamaṃ naiva vidyate | 32|
alābuṃ veṇupātraṃ ca dāravaṃ mṛṇmayaṃ tathā |
bhikṣoścatvāri pātrāṇi pañcamaṃ naiva vidyate | 33|
tāmbūlaṃ taijasaṃ pātraṃ retassekaṃ sitāmbaram |
divāsvāpo hinaktānnaṃ yatīnāṃ ṣaḍvivarjitāḥ | 34|
sākṣarā viparītāśca rākṣasāsta iti smṛtāḥ |
tasmādvai viparītaṃ ca karma naivācared yatiḥ | 35|
yatiḥ prayatnataḥ kuryātkṣaurasnānaṃ ca śuddhaye |
saṃsmaranmanasā śuddhaṃ paraṃ brahma sadāśivam | 36|
ityaiva muniśārdūla tava snehānmayākhilaḥ |
kṣaurasnānavidhiḥ proktaḥ kimbhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi | 37|
iti śrīśivamahāpurāṇe ṣaṣṭhyāṃ kailāsasaṃhitāyāṃ kṣaurasnānavidhivarṇanaṃ nāma viṃśo'dhyāyaḥ | 6.20|
6.21 | śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ | | śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ | | śrīśivamahāpurāṇam |
6.19.d:
सुब्रह्मण्य उवाच ।
क्षौरस्नानविधिं वक्ष्ये वामदेव महामुने ।
यस्य सद्यो विधानेन शुद्धिः स्याद्यतिनः परा । 1।
योगपट्टप्रकारस्य विधिं प्राप्य मुनीश्वर ।
स शिष्यः स्याद् व्रती पूर्णः क्षौरकर्मोद्यतो भवेत् । 2।
गुरुं नत्वा विशेषेण लब्धानुज्ञस्ततो गुरोः ।
शिरः सङ्क्षाल्य चाचम्य सवासाः क्षौरमाचरेत् । 3।
क्षालयेद्वसनं पश्चान्मृदम्भोभिः क्षुरादिकम् ।
तद्धस्तौ च मृदालिप्य क्षालयेति मृदं ददेत् । 4।
स्थापितं प्रोक्षितं तोयैः शिवं शिवमितीरयन् ।
स्वनेत्रे पिहिते चैवानामाङ्गुष्ठाभिमन्त्रिते । 5।
अस्त्रेणोन्मील्य सन्दृश्य क्षुरादिक्षौरसाधनम् ।
अभिमन्त्र्य द्वादशाथ प्रोक्षयेदस्त्रमन्त्रतः । 6।
क्षुरं गृहीत्वा तारेण दक्षभागे निकृन्तयेत् ।
केशांश्च कांश्चिदग्रेषु वप्त्वा सर्वं च वापयेत् । 7।
पृथिव्यां पर्णमादाय विक्षिपेन्न भुवः स्थले ।
श्मश्रूणि हस्तपादस्थनखानि च निकृन्तयेत् । 8।
बिल्वाश्वत्थतुलस्यादिस्थाने सङ्गृह्य मृत्तिकाम् ।
द्विषड्वारं निमज्याप्सु तीरं गत्वोपविश्य च । 9।
शुद्धे देशे तु संस्थाप्य मृदं त्रेधा विभज्य च ।
एवं पुनस्त्रिधा कृत्वा प्रोक्ष्यास्त्रेणाभिमन्त्रयेत् । 6.20.10।
तत्रैकां मृदमादाय दापयित्वान्यपाणिना ।
करौ द्वादशधालिप्य प्रत्येकं केन क्षालयेत् । 11।
पुनरेकां पादयोश्च मुखे चान्यां करे क्रमात् ।
संलिप्याक्षाल्य चाम्भोभिः पुनश्च जलमाविशेत् । 12।
अन्यां मृदं भागयित्वा शिरसि द्वादश क्रमात् ।
आलिप्य मृदमास्यान्तं निमज्य च पुनः पुनः । 13।
तीरं गत्वा तु गण्डूषान् षोडशाचमनं द्विधा ।
प्राणानायम्य च पुनः प्रणवं द्व्यष्टसङ्ख्यया । 14।
मृदमन्यां पुनस्त्रेधा विभज्य च तदेकया ।
कटिशौचं पादशौचं विधायाचम्य च द्विधा । 15।
प्रणवेनाथ षोडश प्राणानायम्य वाग्यतः ।
पुनरन्यां स्वोरुदेशे त्रिधा विन्यस्य चोमिति । 16।
प्रोक्ष्याभिमन्त्रयेत्सप्त स्वपाण्योस्तलमेकधा ।
त्रिधालिप्याथ सम्पश्येत्सूर्यमूर्तिं च पावनीम् । 17।
स्वकक्षयोः समालिप्य व्यत्यस्ताभ्यामथान्यया ।
पाणिभ्यां च मृदा शिष्यः सुमतिर्दृढमानसः । 18।
गृहीत्वान्यां मृदं शुद्धां तथासौ गुरुभक्तिमान् ।
शिर आरभ्य पादान्तं विलिप्यादित्यदृष्टया । 19।
समुत्थाय ततोऽसौ वै दण्डमादाय भूतले ।
स्वगुरुं मन्त्रदं भक्त्या संस्मरेज्ज्ञाननिष्ठया । 6.20.20।
ततः साम्बं महेशानं शङ्करं चन्द्रशेखरम् ।
संस्मरेद्भक्तितः शिष्य सर्वैश्वर्यपतिं शिवम् । 21।
त्रिवारं प्रणमेत्प्रीत्या साष्टाङ्गं च गुरुं शिवम् ।
पञ्चाङ्गेनैकवारं च समुत्थाय च वन्दयेत् । 22।
तीर्थं प्रविश्य तन्मध्ये निमज्योन्मज्य तां मृदम् ।
स्कन्धे संस्थाप्य पूर्वोक्तप्रकारेण विलेपयेत् । 23।
तत्रावशिष्टं सङ्गृह्य जलमध्ये प्रविश्य च ।
विलोड्य सम्यक् तां तत्र सर्वाङ्गेषु विलिप्य च । 24।
त्रिवारमोमिति प्रोच्य शिवपादाम्बुजं स्मरन् ।
संसाराम्बुधिसन्तारं सदा यद्विधितो हि सः । 25।
अभिषिच्योमिति जलं विरजाभस्मलोलितम् ।
अङ्गोपमार्ज्जनं कृत्वा सुस्नायाद्भस्मना ततः । 26।
त्रिपुण्ड्रं च विधायाथ यथोक्तविधिना शुभम् ।
यथोक्ताङ्गेषु सर्वेषु सावधानतया मुने । 27।
ततः शुद्धमना भूत्वा कुर्यान्मध्यदिनक्रियाः ।
महेश्वरं नमस्कृत्य गुरूंस्तीर्थादिकानि च । 28।
सम्पूजयेन्महेशानं भक्त्या परमया मुने ।
साम्बिकं ज्ञानदातारं पातारं त्रिभवस्य वै । 29।
ततोऽसौ दृढचेतस्को यतिः स्ववृषसंस्थितः ।
भिक्षार्थं प्रव्रजेच्छुद्धो विप्रवर्गेषु साधुषु । 6.20.30।
ततस्तत्र च शुद्धात्मा पञ्चधा परिकल्पितम् ।
भैक्ष्यं यथोचितं कुर्याद् दूषितान्नं विवर्जयेत् । 31।
शौचं स्नानं तथा भिक्षां नित्यमेकान्तसेवनम् ।
भिक्षौश्चत्वारि कर्माणि पञ्चमं नैव विद्यते । 32।
अलाबुं वेणुपात्रं च दारवं मृण्मयं तथा ।
भिक्षोश्चत्वारि पात्राणि पञ्चमं नैव विद्यते । 33।
ताम्बूलं तैजसं पात्रं रेतस्सेकं सिताम्बरम् ।
दिवास्वापो हिनक्तान्नं यतीनां षड्विवर्जिताः । 34।
साक्षरा विपरीताश्च राक्षसास्त इति स्मृताः ।
तस्माद्वै विपरीतं च कर्म नैवाचरेद् यतिः । 35।
यतिः प्रयत्नतः कुर्यात्क्षौरस्नानं च शुद्धये ।
संस्मरन्मनसा शुद्धं परं ब्रह्म सदाशिवम् । 36।
इत्यैव मुनिशार्दूल तव स्नेहान्मयाखिलः ।
क्षौरस्नानविधिः प्रोक्तः किम्भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि । 37।
इति श्रीशिवमहापुराणे षष्ठ्यां कैलाससंहितायां क्षौरस्नानविधिवर्णनं नाम विंशोऽध्यायः । 6.20।
6.21 । श्रीगणेशाय नमः । । श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः । । श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ।
6.19.m:
Subrahmaṇya said:
I shall explain the procedure for shaving and bathing, O great sage Vāmadeva, / by the immediate performance of which supreme purity is attained by an ascetic. (1)
Having received the rule for the Yogapaṭṭa ceremony, O foremost of sages, / that disciple, becoming a complete observer of the vow, should prepare for the act of shaving. (2)
Having specially bowed to his guru and then received permission from the guru, / having washed his head and sipped water, he should undergo shaving while wearing his garments. (3)
Afterward, he should wash the clothing, and the razor and other tools, with clay and water; / and rubbing his hands with clay, he should give clay, saying, 'Wash [them].' (4)
Having placed [the items] and sprinkled [them] with water, repeating 'Śiva, Śiva,' / his own eyes being closed, and having consecrated his ring finger and thumb with mantras, (5)
opening [his eyes] with the Astra-mantra and looking at the implements of shaving such as the razor, / and having consecrated them twelve times, he should sprinkle them with the Astra-mantra. (6)
Taking up the razor with the praṇava, he should cut hair on the right side; / and having shaved some hairs at their tips, he should shave all of it. (7)
Receiving them on a leaf upon the ground, he should not scatter them on the earth; / he should also cut the beard and the nails of his hands and feet. (8)
Gathering clay from the place of a bilva, an aśvattha, a tulasī, or similar tree, / and having immersed himself twelve times in water, going to the bank and sitting down (9)
in a pure place, placing the clay and dividing it into three parts, / and having again divided it into three, sprinkling it with the Astra-mantra, he should consecrate it with mantras. (10)
Taking one portion of clay from there and having it given with the other hand, / smearing both hands twelve times, he should wash each with water. (11)
Then [he should smear] one portion on the two feet, another on the mouth, and another on the hand in proper order; / smearing and washing them with water, he should again enter the water. (12)
Dividing another portion of clay, and smearing the clay twelve times in succession upon his head / down to the face, he should dive in repeatedly. (13)
Going to the bank, taking sixteen mouthfuls of water [for rinsing], sipping water twice, / and restraining his breath, [he should recite] the praṇava sixteen times. (14)
Dividing another portion of clay again into three, and with one portion of it / performing purification of the hips and feet, and sipping water twice, (15)
and then with the praṇava, restraining his breath sixteen times with restrained speech, / placing another portion in three parts on the region of his thighs, reciting 'Oṃ,' (16)
he should sprinkle and consecrate it seven times. Smearing the palms of his hands together / three times, he should then gaze upon the purifying form of the sun. (17)
Smearing both his armpits with another portion, crossing his hands, / the disciple, wise and firm-minded, with clay, (18)
taking another pure portion of clay, full of devotion to his guru, / smearing [himself] from head to foot, looking toward the sun, (19)
and then rising, taking up his staff from the ground, / should devotedly remember his guru, the giver of the mantra, through steadfastness in knowledge. (20)
Then the disciple should devotedly remember Śaṅkara, the great lord together with Ambā, / adorned with the crescent moon, Śiva, the master of all sovereignty. (21)
He should bow with affection three times with prostration of eight limbs to his guru and to Śiva, / and rising, he should salute once with five limbs. (22)
Entering the sacred water, diving into its midst, and re-emerging, / placing that clay on his shoulder, he should smear it according to the manner previously stated. (23)
Taking what remains of it, entering the midst of the water, / stirring it well there, and smearing it over all his limbs, (24)
reciting 'Oṃ' three times, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, / which always cross one over the ocean of worldly existence in accordance with the rule, (25)
and pouring over himself water stirred with Virajā ashes, reciting 'Oṃ,' / wiping his limbs, he should then bathe well with ashes. (26)
Then, applying the auspicious tripuṇḍra according to the prescribed rule / upon all the prescribed limbs with attentiveness, O sage, (27)
with a purified mind he should then perform the midday rites, / bowing to Maheśvara, the gurus, the sacred waters, and other holy things. (28)
He should worship the Great Lord with supreme devotion, O sage— / the giver of knowledge together with Ambikā, the protector of the three worlds. (29)
Then that ascetic, with a firm mind, established in his own righteousness, / should wander for alms, purified, among virtuous brahmins. (30)
Then and there, with a pure soul, he should accept alms / prepared in five ways as appropriate, and he should avoid polluted food. (31)
Purification, bathing, alms, and constant dwelling in solitude: / these are the four duties of a mendicant; a fifth does not exist. (32)
A bottle-gourd, a bamboo vessel, a wooden one, and an earthen one: / these are the four begging bowls of a mendicant; a fifth does not exist. (33)
Betel, metallic vessels, emission of semen, white cloth, / sleeping by day, and food at night: these six are avoided by ascetics. (34)
Turned upside down, 'sākṣarāḥ' (the literate) are remembered as 'rākṣasāḥ' (demons); / therefore, an ascetic must never perform contradictory action. (35)
The ascetic should diligently perform shaving and bathing for purity, / remembering in his mind Sadāśiva, the pure, supreme Brahman. (36)
Thus, O tiger among sages, out of affection for you, the entire / procedure for shaving and bathing has been told by me; what more do you wish to hear?
Thus ends the twentieth chapter, titled 'Description of the Procedure for Shaving and Bathing,' in the Kailāsasaṃhitā, the sixth [book] of the holy Śivamahāpurāṇa. (37)
6.21 | Homage to holy Gaṇeśa! | Homage to holy Gaurī and Śaṅkara! | The holy Śivamahāpurāṇa

6.21.s:
vāmadeva uvāca |
ye muktā yatayasteṣāṃ dāhakarma na vidyate |
mṛte śarīre khananaṃ taddehasya śrutaṃ mayā | 1|
tatkarmācakṣva suprītyā kārtikeya guro mama |
tvatto'nyo na hi saṃvaktā triṣu lokeṣu vidyate | 2|
pūrṇāhambhāvamāśritya ye muktā dehapañjarāt |
ye tūpāsanamārgeṇa dehamuktāḥ paraṃ gatāḥ | 3|
teṣāṃ gativiśeṣaṃ ca bhagavan śaṅkarātmaja |
vaktumarhasi suprītyā māṃ vicārya svaśiṣyataḥ | 4|
sūta uvāca |
munivijñaptimākarṇya śaktiputraḥ surārihā |
prāhātyantarahasyaṃ tad bhṛguṇā śrutamīśvarāt | 5|
subrahmaṇya uvāca |
idameva mune guhyaṃ bhṛgave śivayogine |
uktaṃ bhagavatā sākṣātsarvajñena pinākinā | 6|
vakṣye tadadya te brahmanna deyaṃ yasya kasyacit |
deyaṃ śiṣyāya śāntāya śivabhaktiyutāya vai | 7|
6.21.d:
वामदेव उवाच ।
ये मुक्ता यतयस्तेषां दाहकर्म न विद्यते ।
मृते शरीरे खननं तद्देहस्य श्रुतं मया । 1।
तत्कर्माचक्ष्व सुप्रीत्या कार्तिकेय गुरो मम ।
त्वत्तोऽन्यो न हि संवक्ता त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते । 2।
पूर्णाहम्भावमाश्रित्य ये मुक्ता देहपञ्जरात् ।
ये तूपासनमार्गेण देहमुक्ताः परं गताः । 3।
तेषां गतिविशेषं च भगवन् शङ्करात्मज ।
वक्तुमर्हसि सुप्रीत्या मां विचार्य स्वशिष्यतः । 4।
सूत उवाच ।
मुनिविज्ञप्तिमाकर्ण्य शक्तिपुत्रः सुरारिहा ।
प्राहात्यन्तरहस्यं तद् भृगुणा श्रुतमीश्वरात् । 5।
सुब्रह्मण्य उवाच ।
इदमेव मुने गुह्यं भृगवे शिवयोगिने ।
उक्तं भगवता साक्षात्सर्वज्ञेन पिनाकिना । 6।
वक्ष्ये तदद्य ते ब्रह्मन्न देयं यस्य कस्यचित् ।
देयं शिष्याय शान्ताय शिवभक्तियुताय वै । 7।
6.21.m:
Vāmadeva said:
For those ascetics who are liberated, there is no rite of cremation; / I have heard of the burial of their body when the body dies. (1)

Explain that rite with deep affection, O Kārtikeya, my guru; / for there is no speaker other than you in the three worlds. (2)

Those who, taking refuge in the complete sense of 'I', are liberated from the cage of the body, / and those who, through the path of worship, are freed from the body and have attained the Supreme— (3)

the distinction between their destinies, O venerable son of Śaṅkara, / you should graciously declare, regarding me as your own disciple. (4)

Sūta said: / Hearing the sage's request, the son of Śakti, the slayer of the enemies of the gods, / spoke that supreme secret, which Bhṛgu had heard from the Lord.

Subrahmaṇya said: / It was this very secret, O sage, that was spoken to Bhṛgu, the Śiva-yogin, / directly by the venerable, all-knowing Pinākin.

I shall tell it to you today, O sage; it must not be given to just anyone. / It should indeed be given to a peaceful disciple endowed with devotion to Śiva.

6.21.s:
samādhistho yatiḥ kaścicchivabhāvena dehamuk |
asti cetsa mahādhīraḥ paripūrṇaḥ śivo bhavet | 8|
adhairyacitto yaḥ kaścitsamādhiṃ na ca vindati |
tadupāyaṃ pravakṣyāmi sāvadhānatayā śṛṇu | 9|
tripadārthaparijñānaṃ vedāntāgamavākyajam |
śrutvā gurormukhādyogamabhyasetsa yamādikam | 6.21.10|
tatkurvansa yatiḥ samyak śivadhyānaparo bhavet |
niyamena mune nityaṃ praṇavāsaktamānasaḥ | 11|
dehadaurbalyavaśato yadyadhairyadharo yatiḥ |
akāmaśca śivaṃ smṛtvā sa jīrṇāṃ svāṃ tanuṃ tyajet | 12|
sadāśivānugrahato nandinā preritā mune |
ātivāhikarūpiṇyo devatāḥ pañca viśrutāḥ | 13|
agnyahantākṛtiḥ kācijjyottiḥpuñjavapuṣmatī |
ahno'bhimāninī kācicchuklapakṣābhimāninī | 14|
uttarāyaṇarūpā ca pañcānugrahatatparā |
dhūmrā tamasvinī rātriḥ kṛṣṇapakṣābhimāninī | 15|
6.21.d:
समाधिस्थो यतिः कश्चिच्छिवभावेन देहमुक् ।
अस्ति चेत्स महाधीरः परिपूर्णः शिवो भवेत् । 8।
अधैर्यचित्तो यः कश्चित्समाधिं न च विन्दति ।
तदुपायं प्रवक्ष्यामि सावधानतया शृणु । 9।
त्रिपदार्थपरिज्ञानं वेदान्तागमवाक्यजम् ।
श्रुत्वा गुरोर्मुखाद्योगमभ्यसेत्स यमादिकम् । 6.21.10।
तत्कुर्वन्स यतिः सम्यक् शिवध्यानपरो भवेत् ।
नियमेन मुने नित्यं प्रणवासक्तमानसः । 11।
देहदौर्बल्यवशतो यद्यधैर्यधरो यतिः ।
अकामश्च शिवं स्मृत्वा स जीर्णां स्वां तनुं त्यजेत् । 12।
सदाशिवानुग्रहतो नन्दिना प्रेरिता मुने ।
आतिवाहिकरूपिण्यो देवताः पञ्च विश्रुताः । 13।
अग्न्यहन्ताकृतिः काचिज्ज्योत्तिःपुञ्जवपुष्मती ।
अह्नोऽभिमानिनी काचिच्छुक्लपक्षाभिमानिनी । 14।
उत्तरायणरूपा च पञ्चानुग्रहतत्परा ।
धूम्रा तमस्विनी रात्रिः कृष्णपक्षाभिमानिनी । 15।
6.21.m:
If some ascetic, absorbed in samādhi, sheds his body with the consciousness of Śiva, / he, supremely steadfast, becomes the complete Śiva.

If someone whose mind lacks steadfastness does not attain samādhi, / I will state the means for that; listen attentively.

Having heard from the mouth of the guru the comprehensive knowledge of the three realities, born from the statements of the Vedānta and the Āgamas, / he should practice yoga, beginning with the restraints.

Doing that, properly dedicated to meditation on Śiva, / with regularity, O sage, his mind constantly attached to the praṇava,

if the ascetic becomes unsettled in mind through bodily weakness, / free from desire and remembering Śiva, he should abandon his worn-out body.

By the grace of Sadāśiva, dispatched by Nandin, O sage, / five deities taking the form of conductors are renowned:

One has the form of fire and the I-sense, having a body of massed light; / one presides over the day; one presides over the bright fortnight;

and one has the form of the northern solstice—[these] five are intent on bestowing grace. / The smoky, dark night, presiding over the dark fortnight,

6.21.s:
dakṣiṇāyanarūpeti viśrutāḥ pañca devatāḥ |
tāsāṃ vṛttiṃ śṛṇuṣvādya vāmadeva mahāmune | 16|
tāḥ pañca devatā jīvān karmānuṣṭhānatatparān |
gṛhītvā tridivaṃ yānti tatpuṇyavaśato mune | 17|
bhuktvā bhogānyathoktāṃśca te tatpuṇyakṣaye punaḥ |
mānuṣaṃ lokamāsādya bhajate janma pūrvavat | 18|
tāḥ punaḥ pañcadhā mārgaṃ vibhajyārabhya bhūtalam |
agnyādikramatāṃ gṛhya sadāśivapadaṃ yatiḥ | 19|
ninīya vandyacaraṇau devadevasya pṛṣṭhataḥ |
tiṣṭhantyanugrahākārāḥ karmaṇyeva prayojitāḥ | 6.21.20|
samāgatamabhiprekṣya devadevaḥ sadāśivaḥ |

anugṛhṇāti sarveśaḥ śaṅkaraḥ sarvanāyakaḥ | 22|
mṛgaṭaṅkatriśūlāgryavaradānavibhūṣitam |
trinetraṃ candraśakalaṃ gaṅgollāsijaṭādharam | 23|
6.21.d:
दक्षिणायनरूपेति विश्रुताः पञ्च देवताः ।
तासां वृत्तिं शृणुष्वाद्य वामदेव महामुने । 16।
ताः पञ्च देवता जीवान् कर्मानुष्ठानतत्परान् ।
गृहीत्वा त्रिदिवं यान्ति तत्पुण्यवशतो मुने । 17।
भुक्त्वा भोगान्यथोक्तांश्च ते तत्पुण्यक्षये पुनः ।
मानुषं लोकमासाद्य भजते जन्म पूर्ववत् । 18।
ताः पुनः पञ्चधा मार्गं विभज्यारभ्य भूतलम् ।
अग्न्यादिक्रमतां गृह्य सदाशिवपदं यतिः । 19।
निनीय वन्द्यचरणौ देवदेवस्य पृष्ठतः ।
तिष्ठन्त्यनुग्रहाकाराः कर्मण्येव प्रयोजिताः । 6.21.20।
समागतमभिप्रेक्ष्य देवदेवः सदाशिवः ।
विरक्तश्चेन्महामन्त्रतात्पर्यमुपदिश्य च । 21।
स्वसाम्यं च वपुर्दत्ते गाणपत्येभिषिच्य च ।
अनुगृह्णाति सर्वेशः शङ्करः सर्वनायकः । 22।
मृगटङ्कत्रिशूलाग्र्यवरदानविभूषितम् ।
त्रिनेत्रं चन्द्रशकलं गङ्गोल्लासिजटाधरम् । 23।
6.21.m:
and having the form of the southern solstice—thus five deities are renowned. / Hear their function today, O great sage Vāmadeva.

Those five deities take the individual souls dedicated to performing rituals / and go to heaven in accordance with their merit, O sage.

Having enjoyed the pleasures as prescribed, when that merit is exhausted, / reaching the human world again, they undergo birth as before.

Dividing the path into five, beginning from the earth, / and taking the sequence of fire and the rest, the ascetic reaches the abode of Sadāśiva.

Having led [him], standing behind the adorable feet of the God of gods, / having the form of grace, they are employed in their very duty.

Seeing that he has arrived, the God of gods, Sadāśiva, / if he is detached, instructs him in the import of the great mantra,

and grants him a body equal to his own, and having consecrated him in the lordship of the attendants, / the lord of all, Śaṅkara, the leader of all, bestows his grace.

[Granting a chariot] adorned with the deer, the axe, the trident, and the bestowing of boons, / three-eyed, [marked by] the crescent moon, bearing matted locks adorned by the surging Gaṅgā,

6.21.s:
adhiṣṭhitavimānāgryaṃ sarvagaṃ sarvakāmadam |
iti śākhāviraktasya rudrakanyāsamāvṛtam | 24|
nṛtyagītamṛdaṅgādivādyaghoṣamanoharam |
divyāmbarasragālepabhūṣaṇairapi bhūṣitam | 25|
divyāmṛtaghaṭaiḥ pūrṇaṃ divyāmbhaḥparipūritam |
sūryakoṭipratīkāśaṃ candrakoṭisuśītalam | 26|
manovegaṃ sarvagaṃ ca vimānamanugṛhya ca |
bhuktabhogasya tasyāpi bhogakautūhalakṣaye | 27|
nipātya śaktiṃ tīvratarāṃ prakṛtyā hyatidurgamām |
kāntāraṃ dagdhukāmāṃ tāṃ pralayānalasuprabhām | 28|

pūrṇo'haṃ bhāvanārūpaḥ śambhurasmīti niścalam | 29|

ravyādikarmmasāmarthyarūpāḥ siddhīranargalāḥ | 6.21.30|
āyuḥkṣaye padmayoneḥ punarāvṛttivarjitām |
muktiṃ ca paramāṃ tasmai prayacchati jagadguruḥ | 31|
6.21.d:
अधिष्ठितविमानाग्र्यं सर्वगं सर्वकामदम् ।
इति शाखाविरक्तस्य रुद्रकन्यासमावृतम् । 24।
नृत्यगीतमृदङ्गादिवाद्यघोषमनोहरम् ।
दिव्याम्बरस्रगालेपभूषणैरपि भूषितम् । 25।
दिव्यामृतघटैः पूर्णं दिव्याम्भःपरिपूरितम् ।
सूर्यकोटिप्रतीकाशं चन्द्रकोटिसुशीतलम् । 26।
मनोवेगं सर्वगं च विमानमनुगृह्य च ।
भुक्तभोगस्य तस्यापि भोगकौतूहलक्षये । 27।
निपात्य शक्तिं तीव्रतरां प्रकृत्या ह्यतिदुर्गमाम् ।
कान्तारं दग्धुकामां तां प्रलयानलसुप्रभाम् । 28।
अनुगृह्य महामन्त्रतात्पर्यं परमेश्वरः ।
पूर्णोऽहं भावनारूपः शम्भुरस्मीति निश्चलम् । 29।
अनुगृह्य समाधिं च स्वदास्यस्पन्दरूपिणीः ।
रव्यादिकर्म्मसामर्थ्यरूपाः सिद्धीरनर्गलाः । 6.21.30।
आयुःक्षये पद्मयोनेः पुनरावृत्तिवर्जिताम् ।
मुक्तिं च परमां तस्मै प्रयच्छति जगद्गुरुः । 31।

6.21.s:
